C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Luis Walter Alvarez is a physicist. Alvarez devised a set of experiments to observe K-electron capture in radioactive nuclei, predicted by the beta decay theory but never before observed.
Which of these is a chemist?
Chaim Weizmann is a chemist. As a biochemist, Weizmann is considered to be the 'father' of industrial fermentation.
What is the atomic number of Unbihexium?
Unbihexium, also known as element 126 or eka-plutonium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has atomic number 126 and placeholder symbol Ubh.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
Which company manufactures LTV A-7 Corsair II?
LTV A-7 Corsair II: Ling-Temco-Vought. The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).
Which country is Sukhoi Su-57 from?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russia. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
This English academic and broadcaster, an anatomist and archaeologist by training, was president of the charity Humanists UK from 2019 to 2022 — who is she?
Alice Roberts (born 19 May 1973) is an English academic, anatomist, archaeologist, TV presenter and author.

Its name means 'unlike other shrimp.' Known best from the Burgess Shale, this extinct radiodont swam with body flaps and stared out through huge compound eyes packed with lenses — what was this stem-arthropod?

Anomalocaris (from Ancient Greek, meaning "anomalous", and, meaning "shrimp", with the intended meaning "unlike other shrimp") is an extinct genus of radiodont, an order of early-diverging stem-group marine arthropods.
This genus of roughly 300 evergreen flowering plants includes one edible species enjoyed as a vegetable and another grown purely as an ornamental — which genus?
Asparagus (genus) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Asparagoideae.
Six carbons in a flat hexagonal ring, each wearing a single hydrogen — this textbook aromatic hydrocarbon has the formula C6H6 — what is it?
Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
This Russian mathematician-turned-oligarch was worth an estimated $3 billion in 1997 after privatizing state assets like Channel One — yet died impoverished and depressed in 2013. Who was he?
Boris Berezovsky (businessman) (23 January 1946 - 23 March 2013), also known as Platon Elenin, was a Russian business oligarch, government official, engineer and mathematician.
The very same compound that hardens eggshells, builds pearls, and forms the chalk on a classroom board can also be swallowed as an antacid to calm an upset stomach — what is it?
Calcium carbonate is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CaCO3.
This set of metabolic reactions oxidizes biological fuels using an electron acceptor like oxygen to produce ATP, the molecule that stores usable chemical energy in cells — what is it?

Cellular respiration is the process of oxidizing biological fuels using an inorganic electron acceptor, such as oxygen, to drive production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

An organic compound found naturally in citrus fruits with the formula C6H8O7, over two million tons are manufactured annually for use as an acidifier, flavoring, and preservative. What is this compound?
Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7. In biochemistry, it is an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, which occurs in the metabolism of all aerobic organisms.
Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
This Penn professor's discoveries about modified nucleosides made the Pfizer and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible, earning him a share of the 2023 Nobel Prize in Medicine — who is he?
Drew Weissman (born September 7, 1959) is an American physician and immunologist known for his contributions to RNA biology.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Cats in this subfamily can purr but never roar, thanks to a bony rather than flexible hyoid bone — which subfamily?
Felinae are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.

A spiny mammal with 17 species across five genera in Europe, Asia, and Africa, this creature shares distant ancestry with shrews. There are no native populations in Australia or the Americas, though one extinct genus once roamed North America—what is it?
Hedgehog is a spiny mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.
Petroleum, natural gas, and coal all fall under which class of organic compound built solely from hydrogen and carbon, spanning gases, liquids, waxes, and polymers?
Hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.

This analytical framework, which arose partly in reaction to both white feminism and the male-dominated Black liberation movement, examines how overlapping social identities create unique combinations of discrimination and privilege — name the concept?
Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege.
This financier's 1999 bestseller on mutual funds became an investment classic after he founded a low-cost investing giant — who is he?

John C. Bogle (May 8, 1929 - January 16, 2019) was an American investor, business magnate and philanthropist who was the founder of The Vanguard Group and is credited with popularizing the index fund.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).
At the time of her death, this French heiress and cosmetics-empire shareholder was the richest woman in the world, worth over $44 billion. Who is she?
Liliane Bettencourt (ne Schueller; 21 October 1922 - 21 September 2017) was a French heiress, socialite and businesswoman.
Which group of vividly colored, long-tailed New World parrots — prized in aviculture though some species face conservation concerns — belongs to the tribe Arini?
Macaw are a group of large New World parrots that are long-tailed and often colorful, in the tribe Arini.
Ranging from Patagonia to Bolivia during the Ice Age, this genus of giant ground sloths includes a type species that could weigh nearly four tonnes — which genus?

Megatherium (meg--; from Greek mga 'great' + theron 'beast') is an extinct genus of large ground sloths endemic to South America that lived from the Early Pliocene through the end of the Late Pleistocene.
The dried leaves of this Southeast Asian evergreen tree, known as kratom, contain alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors as partial agonists. What plant is it?
Mitragyna speciosa is a tropical evergreen tree of the Rubiaceae family native to Southeast Asia.
This genus of spring-blooming perennials in the amaryllis family is better known by common names like daffodil and jonquil, with trumpet-shaped flowers usually white and yellow. What is it?
Narcissus (plant) is a genus of predominantly spring flowering perennial plants of the amaryllis family, Amaryllidaceae.
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.

This genus of fragrant flowering shrubs, native to Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean, is widely grown as an ornamental in Hawaii and in desert climates of the Arabian Peninsula — name the genus?
Plumeria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
The only member of the genus Rangifer, this circumpolar deer of the Arctic tundra goes by another name entirely in North America — what is it?
Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.
A botanist active in Japan's Meiji era, this scholar died in 1899 after decades of scientific work — who was he?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (October 13, 1851 - August 8, 1899) was a Japanese botanist during the Meiji era.
This veteran of six spaceflights was the first Russian cosmonaut to fly aboard NASA's Space Shuttle, on mission STS-60 — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev (born 27 August 1958) is a Russian mechanical engineer and former cosmonaut.
Made simply from ice mixed with fruit juice or purée, plus the occasional splash of wine or honey, this dairy-free frozen treat goes by what name?
Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit pure, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

This unit of time is based on how long Earth takes to complete one full orbit around the Sun, with the precise scientific definition running about 365 days, 5 hours, and 48 minutes — what unit is this?

Year is a unit of time based on how long it takes the Earth to orbit the Sun. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Native to North America but now invasive across Europe after being introduced, this semiaquatic mustelid preys on rodents, fish, and frogs — which animal?
American mink: Semiaquatic species of mustelid. Because of range expansion, the American mink is classed as a least-concern species by the IUCN.
Nicknamed "the heart of the scorpion," this reddish supergiant is the brightest star in its constellation — what is it?
Antares: Binary star in the constellation Scorpius.
Pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon in 2003, this mountaineer amputated his own forearm with a dull pocket knife to survive, later portrayed by James Franco in a film — who is he?
Delivered to the RAF starting in 1956, this delta-wing strategic bomber was considered the most advanced but riskiest of Britain's three V bombers — which aircraft?
Avro Vulcan: British jet-powered delta wing strategic bomber.
This common, noncancerous enlargement of a male gland can cause frequent urination and a weak stream; it isn't linked to poor hygiene, and there's no known cure. What's the condition?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Composed of plasma plus red cells, white cells, and platelets, this circulatory fluid delivers oxygen and nutrients to the body while carrying away waste — what is it?
Blood: Body fluid in the circulatory system. Plasma, which constitutes 55% of blood fluid, is mostly water (92% by volume), and contains proteins, glucose, mineral ions, and hormones.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.
This human-feeding ectoparasite is one of the world's great "nuisance pests" — yet despite carrying dozens of pathogens, no study has shown it transmits any disease to us. What is it?
Cimex lectularius: Species of true bug.
This medical term describes inflammation of the large intestine, used both when the cause is undiagnosed and for its specific ulcerative form — what condition is it?
Colitis: Inflammation of the colon (large intestine). Colitis may be acute and self-limited or long-term.
Home to crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, this bird family boasts a brain-to-body ratio rivaling great apes, and one of its members even passed the mirror self-recognition test — what family is this?

A Scottish biologist, classicist and mathematician who pioneered theoretical biology, he's remembered for his 1917 book On Growth and Form, which opened the way to explaining how patterns and body structures take shape — who was he?
D'Arcy Wentworth Thompson: Scottish biologist, mathematician, and classics scholar.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a single day, this condition is most often caused by an intestinal infection from contaminated food or water — what is it?

Diarrhea: Loose or liquid bowel movements. Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
Element 105 sparked a long Cold War naming dispute, claimed first by a Soviet institute in 1968 and then by Berkeley in 1970 before being settled in 1993 — which synthetic element?
Dubnium: Chemical element with atomic number 105 (Db)
The second-largest member of the deer family, this animal is also called "wapiti," a Shawnee and Cree word meaning "white rump" for the pale fur it flashes to signal alarm — what animal is it?
Elk: Species of deer. The word "elk" originally referred to the European variety of the moose, Alces alces, but was transferred to Cervus canadensis by North American colonists.

In 2019 this French-American MIT economist shared the Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty, rooted in the randomized trials of her J-PAL lab — who is she?
This front-of-the-head body part houses most sense organs — eyes, nose, and mouth — and its damage or scarring can profoundly affect a person's sense of identity. What is it?
Face: Front of a head. The face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
Belonging to a bird family that's the only survivor of its order, this wading bird comes in four American species plus two more across Africa and Eurasia — what is it?
Flamingo: Family of birds. There are four flamingo species distributed throughout the Americas (including the Caribbean), and two species native to Afro-Eurasia.
Known as the brain's chief inhibitory neurotransmitter, this compound is also sold as a dietary supplement despite debate over whether it crosses the blood-brain barrier — what is it?
GABA: Main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain.
Ranging from eastern Bangladesh to Southeast Asia, these tailless 'lesser apes' swing branch to branch at speeds up to 55 km/h (34 mph) — what are they?
Gibbon: Family of apes. The family historically contained one genus, but now is split into four extant genera and 20 species.
The largest and most widespread member of its rosy-pink family, this wading bird ranges from Sub-Saharan Africa to the Mediterranean and Central Asia — which species?
In music theory, this concept for combining different pitches into chords and progressions has both a 'vertical' frequency dimension and a 'horizontal' time dimension — what is it called?
Harmony: Aspect of music. In music, harmony is the concept of combining different sounds in order to create new, distinct musical ideas.

This American philosopher co-created an algorithm for the Boolean satisfiability problem and helped prove Hilbert's tenth problem unsolvable — all while reshaping the philosophy of mind and language. Who was he?
Hilary Putnam: American mathematician and philosopher (1926–2016)
Marketed under the brand name Plaquenil, this oral medication treats malaria as well as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, though it can cause retinopathy with long-term use — what drug is it?
Hydroxychloroquine: Antimalarial medication. It is taken by mouth, often in the form of hydroxychloroquine sulfate.

According to psychologist Alfred Adler, this persistent feeling of being deficient or lesser than others — often stemming from childhood comparisons to a sibling — can lead people to overcompensate. What is it called?
Inferiority complex: Intense feeling of inadequacy and inferior.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented a global team sport, wrote its original rule book, and founded the University of Kansas's program for it in 1898 — who is he?

An Alberta-born clinical psychologist and University of Toronto professor, he drew huge attention in the late 2010s for his cultural and political views — self-identifying as a classical liberal. Who is he?

Also called 47,XXY, this chromosome anomaly leaves those affected phenotypically male but often infertile, and is named after the American endocrinologist who first identified it in the 1940s — what's the condition?

An Atlanta factory superintendent with a Cornell engineering degree, he was wrongly convicted of murdering a young employee, then kidnapped from prison and lynched — a case that became a focus of antisemitism. Who was he?
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.

Endemic to North America and known for long, upward-curving upper tusks with little to no lower tusks, this proboscidean's genus split from other elephant relatives at least 28 million years ago — which ancient beast?
In medicine, this term describes a disease spreading from a primary site to a secondary one — most often used for a cancer seeding new tumors elsewhere in the body — what is it?
Metastasis: Spreading of a disease inside a body. The newly pathological sites, then, are metastases (mets).
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
This Austrian-School economist founded anarcho-capitalism and called the state "the organization of robbery systematized and writ large" — which libertarian theoretician?
The sole species in its genus and a fixture of Mediterranean gardens, this drought-and-flood-tolerant shrub of the dogbane family is also called rose laurel or rosebay — what is it?
Nerium: Species of plant. It is the only species currently classified in the genus Nerium, belonging to subfamily Apocynoideae of the dogbane family Apocynaceae.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Nicknamed 'brittle bone disease,' this genetic disorder causes fragile bones and blue-tinted eye whites, usually stemming from faulty type I collagen — what is it?
Osteogenesis imperfecta: Group of genetic disorders resulting in fragile bones.

Also called the blue passionflower, this South American vine climbs via tendrils to 10 metres, bears fragrant blue-white blooms with a fringed coronal filament, and produces an edible but not particularly tasty orange fruit — which plant is it?
Passiflora caerulea: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
Its Nahuatl name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' but this spineless desert cactus is better known for containing the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what is it?
Peyote: Species of psychoactive cactus. Peyote, also known as Lophophora williamsii, is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.
This self-limiting skin condition begins with a single “herald patch” before smaller scaly spots erupt days later, usually clearing up on its own within three months — which condition?
Pityriasis rosea: Skin disease. It usually lasts less than three months and goes away without treatment.
Used to disinfect skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can cause kidney problems and high blood sodium if applied to large wounds, and comes as a liquid, ointment, or powder — what is it?
Povidone-iodine: Antiseptic solution. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.
Broader than linguistics, this field studies how signs — from words to maps to clothing — form systems that carry meaning, split into syntactics, semantics, and pragmatics — what is it called?
Semiotics: Study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
Living in damp spots like rotting wood, these polyphyletic organisms combine into fruiting bodies that release spores to help decompose dead plants — what are they?
Native to China and Vietnam but now invasive across the US after spreading through South Korea and Japan, this planthopper prefers the also-invasive tree of heaven as its host — what insect is it?
Spotted lanternfly: Species of planthopper indigenous to Southeast Asia.
A colorless, non-toxic gas with an octahedral, six-fluorine structure, it's over 23,000 times worse for the climate than CO2 — which hypervalent compound is it?
Sulfur hexafluoride: Chemical compound and greenhouse gas.
Which calculus result approximates a differentiable function near a point using a polynomial — its first-order version being the familiar linear approximation?

Taylor's theorem: Approximation of a function by a polynomial. There are several versions of Taylor's theorem, some giving explicit estimates of the approximation error of the function by its Taylor polynomial.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
Which mathematical principle states that, for any three-sided shape, the sum of two side lengths must be at least as long as the third?
Triangle inequality: Property of geometry, also used to generalize the notion of "distance" in metric spaces.
This genus of flowering plants, whose stinging hairs give it the common name 'stinging nettle,' takes its scientific name from the Latin word for 'sting' — what is it?
Urtica: Genus of flowering plants. Due to the stinging hairs, Urtica are rarely eaten by herbivores, but provide shelter for insects.
Born in Omaha to a U.S. congressman, this investor chairs Berkshire Hathaway and ranked as the world's ninth-richest person in early 2026 — who is he?
Warren Buffett: American investor and philanthropist (born 1930)
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
The symbol for dysprosium is Dy. Dysprosium is a chemical element; it has symbol Dy and atomic number 66.
What is the chemical symbol for krypton?
The symbol for krypton is Kr. Krypton is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

James Nesbitt is a comedian. William James Nesbitt (born 15 January 1965) is an actor from Northern Ireland.
In what year was Joey King born?
Joey King: Joey Lynn King (born July 30, 1999) is an American actress.
In what year was Tony Curtis born?
Tony Curtis: In his later years, Curtis made numerous television appearances.
In what year was Sarah Michelle Gellar born?
Sarah Michelle Gellar: Sarah Michelle Prinze (née Gellar GHEL-ər; born April 14, 1977) is an American actress.
In what year was Tilda Swinton born?
Tilda Swinton: Katherine Matilda "Tilda" Swinton (born 5 November 1960) is a Scottish actress.
In what year was Viola Davis born?
Viola Davis ( vy-OH-lə; born August 11, 1965) is an American actress and film producer.
In what year was Woody Allen born?
